t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a deep navy background with a soft warm light leak at the top right. Mono breadcrumb and light-weight sans-serif headline top left. Centre: a soft 3D studio render of white polypropylene equipment with translucent water in cylindrical housings on a white plinth, soft contact shadow. Glowing steel-blue hotspot dots on the equipment connect by thin right-angle leader lines to limestone cards with mono numbered eyebrows and plus icons. A row of four equal cards across the bottom for <CONTENT>. Faint dimension ticks in the negative space.
signature_idea: The skid itself is the index: hotspots on a white PP render lead to the document each part generates.
strengths: ties each document to physical equipment, good for validation readers
white PP render shows the material story directly
cards with mono eyebrows and plus icons translate to an accordion/card component
light headline and navy ground on-brand
weaknesses: duplicate cards (top and bottom repeat) cause confusion
glossy render with drop shadows and warm glow is softer and more consumer than the line-art brand
hype copy invented by the model ('Seamless validation', compliance badges) violates voice
rounded-looking soft shadows and pills drift from square, flat system
render is costly to produce for real
brand_fit_why: Navy, limestone cards, light headline and mono labels fit, but the glossy 3D render, glows, shadows and pill badges are softer and more decorative than the precise, flat, square brand.
